title: Pitch based anatomy fitting: Prospective Study in SSD CI recipients
summary:
People with a cochlear implant who are deaf in one ear often describe the sound they hear as “tinny” or very high-pitched. Especially in situations where there is a lot of background noise or the acoustics are poor (such as when several people are talking at once), the CI may not always provide adequate assistance. When it comes to music, many users report that it sounds unpleasant. One possible reason for this is that the way sounds are processed in the CI is not optimal. Sometimes the location where electrical stimulation occurs is far removed from where sounds are normally perceived in the ear. In some cases, this difference can even exceed two “octaves,” making it difficult to listen to music. It is believed that these issues arise because the transmission of acoustic frequencies via the cochlear implant is subject to certain shifts and distortions. We would like to test two new methods to better customize and optimize the cochlear implant (CI).
First method: Anatomy-based CI speech processor fitting, in which the position of the individual electrode contacts in the cochlea is determined using routine postoperative CT images. These then serve as the basis for the frequency distribution in the CI-speech processor. 
Second method: Pitch-based CI speech processor tuning, determined by matching the pitch to the normal-hearing contralateral ear.
Through these two customized settings of the CI processor, we hope to improve speech understanding in challenging listening situations (e.g., in noisy environments) and enhance sound quality.
conditions: Conductive hearing loss, unilateral with unrestricted hearing on the contralateral side
Presence of otological and audiological implants
Fitting and adjustment of other devices related to nervous system and special senses

interventions.name: 1. Anatomy-based CI processor fitting based on postoperative imaging (photon-counting CT).
2. Pitch-based CI processor fitting based on a pitch comparison test with the normal-hearing contralateral ear.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-SSD CI recipients, near normal hearing in the opposite ear (pure tone air conduction
equal or less 30 dB HL 500 Hz - 1 kHz, equal or less 40 dB HL 2 - 8 kHz).
-CI-processor programming allows setting of customized filter bank: support of individual frequency mapping is realized with Otoplan 4 and MAESTRO 9 / 10 / 11 (MED-EL, Innsbruck, Austria). Only patients provided with products of this manufacturer will be included.
-Duration of deafness less than 15 years.
-Sufficient proficiency of German language for speech perception tests.
-Angle of insertion of the most apical electrode at least 540 degrees
-Minimum number of active channels: 11
-MED-EL FLEX Electrodes, Synchrony 2 Implants, Flex 28 and Flexsoft electrodes, 
-CI-Processors: Sonnet 2, Sonnet 3 or Rondo 3.
-No prior experience of PBF/ABF filter settings or participation in the 'INDICI' study.
-Willingness to use PBF/ABF fitting on a daily basis during 2 accommodation interval.
Exclusion criteria:
-Congenital unilateral deafness or congenital unilateral profound hearing loss.
-Partial insertion of CI-electrode: Cases with electrode tip foldover or other anomalous deviation of electrodeplacement are excluded.
-CI-Non user (does not accept CI at all).
-Compromised auditory nerve (e.g. patients post severe head trauma or severe meningitis). 
-Malformations of the cochlea.
-Stimulation of the facial nerve.
